result:
Don't split yet: keep one deployable app and turn it into a modular monolith with enforced team boundaries, moving to micro-frontends only if independent deployment is the specific thing blocking you.

Micro-frontends buy you independent releases and fault isolation per team, but you pay for them with runtime integration complexity: shared dependency versioning, duplicated bundles, cross-app routing, auth and state, and failures that only show up in production composition.

Most of the pain five teams feel in one app (unclear ownership, merge conflicts, slow CI, accidental coupling) is fixed more cheaply by a monorepo with per-team packages, CODEOWNERS, lint-enforced import boundaries, and affected-only builds with caching (Nx or Turborepo).

Those boundaries are also the prerequisite for a split, so the work is not wasted if you later carve out a slice with Module Federation.

The recommendation flips if teams are regularly blocked for days waiting on each other's releases even with feature flags and a fast release train, or if a team needs a different stack or release cadence for regulatory or acquisition reasons. In that case, split out only that team's vertical slice first rather than all five.
